title: Temperature-Controlled Lower Deck Compartment for Pharmaceutical Traffic
abstract: Operator request for an actively cooled lower deck compartment to carry temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical freight, placed on hold pending a business case that the requested fleet size does not currently support.

sections.request: We have been asked by two freight forwarders to carry pharmaceutical shipments that must be held between two and eight degrees for the whole flight. Today we can only warm the compartment, not cool it, so we are limited to shipper-provided active containers, and those containers eat payload and cost our customers more than they want to pay. We would like the aft compartment of four of our aircraft to be able to hold a set temperature band on its own, with a readout in the cockpit and a recorded temperature trace we can give to the customer after the flight. We understand this is not a small change. What we need first is an indication of whether it is possible at all on this aircraft and roughly what it would cost, so that we can decide whether to pursue it.
sections.background: We have carried this traffic on wet-leased freighters for two seasons and the margins are good, but the lessor is withdrawing the aircraft in 2027. Our own aircraft are configured for passenger operation with a bulk aft compartment. We have looked at the container route and the payload penalty is between 900 and 1 400 kilogrammes per shipment, which removes most of the margin on our sector lengths.
sections.expected_outcome: A feasibility answer and a budgetary figure within six months, covering four aircraft, so that the commercial team can decide whether to commit before the wet lease ends.

type_data.business_justification: The operator projects 6 MEUR of annual freight revenue but only over four aircraft; the non-recurring cost of a certified active cooling installation cannot be recovered over that fleet size at the sector lengths flown.
type_data.closure_note: Placed on hold in June 2026 after the feasibility study returned a non-recurring cost of 11.4 MEUR for a certified active cooling installation in the aft lower deck compartment, against a four-aircraft fleet. The study confirmed that the compartment can be cooled within the existing pack margin, so the technical route is open, but the operator cannot recover the non-recurring cost at the sector lengths flown. The order will be re-opened if the operator commits a further six aircraft or if a second customer joins the development, and the feasibility work is retained so that neither case has to start again.
